method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 80 covers 36th-39th (avenues O 1/2, P, P 1/2, Q), sheet 90 covers 39th-42nd (avenues S 1/2, T, T 1/2). 39th St is the only corridor both plates draw, and both print '39TH ST.' in it. CAVEAT, recorded not hidden: the two sheets do NOT overlap in x - sheet 80 ends at Avenue Q and sheet 90 begins at Avenue S 1/2, about two plate-widths further east - so this control constrains the cross-street (y) registration only, not x. Identity is nevertheless certain from the continuous hundred-block chain along 39th: sheet 80's north frontage reads 1802 1804 1806 1808 1810 1812 | 1814 1816 1818 1820 1822 1824 (the Avenue O 1/2 to Avenue P block, 20' alley) and then 1902 1904 1906 1908 1910 east of Avenue P, so O1/2=1800 and P=1900; carrying that on gives P1/2=2000, Q=2100, Q1/2=2200, R=2300, R1/2=2400, S=2500, S1/2=2600, T=2700 - and sheet 90's south frontage of 39th reads 2701 2703 2705 ... 2725 2727 2729 then 2801 2803 2805 2807 across Av. T 1/2, exactly as predicted. Sheet 80's next street north is 38th, sheet 90's next south is 40th, so no off-by-one is possible. Detection's candidates (80: 2985/1833/682; 90: 1016/2152/3288) were discarded. Positions are the mid-line of the 80' corridor (the width is printed on sheet 80): sheet 80 faces y=3558 and y=3797 -> 3677; sheet 90 faces y=93 and y=332 -> 213.
